groups.title: Mucolytic Expectorant Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to break down mucus and help bring up phlegm in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: For adults, take 300 mg by mouth per dose, 2 to 3 times a day. When it is used for acute respiratory disease, do not take it for 10 days or more in a row.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be given to people who are hypersensitive to it, or who have liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment. Before taking it, people with mild or moderate liver impairment, people with diabetes or on a low-calorie diet (syrup form only), people who have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5, women who are or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Mucus breakdown and expectoration in acute and chronic respiratory disease
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Liver or kidney disease; peptic ulcer; pregnancy or breastfeeding

groups.title: Vitamin C, Zinc and Selenium Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamin C and to supply zinc and selenium in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding, and when strength is low during or after illness.
groups.usage: For people aged 12 years and over and adults, take 1 tablet per dose 2 times a day, or 2 tablets per dose once a day.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by infants under 12 months of age, or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, people with hyperoxaluria (too much oxalate passed in the urine), women who are or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, premature babies, infants and people with peptic ulcer should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin C, zinc and selenium supply
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Infants under 12 months; hyperoxaluria; peptic ulcer

groups.title: Multivitamin Tablet with Iron
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamins A, B1, B2, B6, C, D and E in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding, when strength is low during or after illness, during growth periods and in old age. It is also used to relieve dry eyes and night blindness, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: For children aged 8 years and over and adults, 1 tablet per dose, once a day.
groups.caution: Taking 5000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects, so women within the first 3 months of pregnancy and women who may be pregnant must not take this medicine. An overdose in children aged 6 years or under may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children. It must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it or who have hypercalcaemia (too much calcium in the blood). Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin A, B, C, D and E supply; dry eyes, night blindness; iron deficiency anaemia
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Pregnancy or possible pregnancy; children (risk of iron poisoning)

groups.title: Multivitamin Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding, when strength is low during or after illness, during growth periods and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (such as low back pain and stiff shoulders), angular stomatitis, cheilitis and other such symptoms.
groups.usage: For people aged 12 years and over and adults, 1 tablet per dose, once a day.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it or to soybean oil, soy or peanuts, by people with hypercalcaemia (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure, or by infants under 12 months of age. Before taking it, women who are or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin D, E, B and C supply; bone and tooth development; neuralgia and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Soy or peanut allergy; high blood calcium; kidney disease or stones

groups.title: Digestive Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for indigestion, poor appetite, overeating, a feeling of food stuck in the stomach, to help digestion, and for a bloated feeling in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 tablets per dose, 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by children aged 7 years and under or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, women who are or may be pregnant, people with an allergic constitution, and people who are or have been hypersensitive to Yellow No. 4 should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage.

summaryTable.Use: Indigestion, poor appetite, overeating, bloating after eating
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years and under; pregnancy; dye allergy

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after trauma or surgery, and infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: For adults, take 300 mg by mouth per dose, 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 1200 mg a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. This medicine may increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. It must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it or who have a stomach ulcer. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis and joint inflammation; pain and swelling after injury or surgery
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Regular alcohol use; heart, blood vessel or stomach problems

groups.title: Cold Relief Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose, 3 times a day; for children over 7 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: runny nose, congestion, sore throat, cough, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; regular alcohol use; skin rash after taking

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin B, C, D and E supply; neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, mouth and skin symptoms
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Infants under 12 months; high blood calcium; kidney disease or stones

groups.title: Analgesic and Antipyretic Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and to reduce fever with chills.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 tablet per dose, up to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Headache, toothache, joint and muscle pain, period pain; fever with chills
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; regular alcohol use; skin rash after taking

groups.title: Vitamin B6 Tablet

groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by infants under 3 months of age, or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, infants under 1 year of age and people who are short of folic acid should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage. When it is given to a child, an adult should supervise.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin B6 supply; mouth and lip inflammation, eczema, dermatitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Infants under 3 months; low folic acid

Before taking it, children aged 10 years and under, women who are or may be pregnant, people with severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, people on a sodium-restricted diet, and people who have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Constipation and the poor appetite, bloating and haemorrhoids that come with it

groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for difficulty in bringing up phlegm in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For acute disease: adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose, 3 times a day; children aged 6 to 14 years take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose, 2 times a day; and children aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water. For chronic disease: adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose, 2 times a day, and children aged 6 to 14 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis: people aged 6 years and over take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, and children aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) per dose, 4 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution: This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so people with phenylketonuria who need to limit their phenylalanine intake must not take it. It must also not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by people with gastric or duodenal ulcer, or by infants under 2 years of age. Before taking it, women who are or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Phenylketonuria; infants under 2 years; stomach or duodenal ulcer

groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding, when strength is low during or after illness, during growth periods and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (such as low back pain and stiff shoulders), angular stomatitis, cheilitis and other such symptoms.
groups.usage: For people aged 12 years and over and adults, 1 tablet per dose, once a day.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by people with hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney stones or severe kidney failure, by infants under 12 months of age, or by people who have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil or who are hypersensitive to soy or peanuts. Before taking it, people who are under a doctor's care, people with hyperoxaluria, women who are or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, premature babies and infants should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin D, E, B and C supply; bone and tooth development; neuralgia and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Soy or peanut allergy; high blood calcium; kidney stones

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis and ankylosing spondylitis. It is also used as supportive treatment for painful swelling or inflammation after trauma or surgery and for infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet per dose, 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 tablets a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. This medicine may increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. People with uncontrolled high blood pressure or congestive heart failure should take particular care. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis and joint inflammation; pain and swelling after injury or surgery
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Regular alcohol use; heart, blood vessel or stomach problems

groups.title: Antacid and Laxative Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for its antacid action and to improve symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for constipation.
groups.usage: For gastric or duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, 2 to 4 tablets (0.5 to 1 g) a day in several divided doses; for constipation, 8 tablets (2 g) a day in 1 to 2 divided doses. Take the smallest amount for the first dose, then increase or decrease it a little at a time while watching the form and condition of the stools.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people with kidney problems or diarrhoea. Before taking it, people with impaired heart function, people with high blood magnesium and older people aged 65 years and over should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it together with tetracycline antibiotics. If you take it with large amounts of milk or with calcium products, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Antacid action for ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid; constipation
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Kidney problems; diarrhoea; age 65 years and over; other medicines

groups.title: Vitamin B1 and B6 Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamins B1 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding and when strength is low during or after illness, and to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (such as low back pain and stiff shoulders), beriberi, eye strain, angular stomatitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: For people aged 12 years and over and adults, take 1 tablet per dose 2 times a day, or 2 tablets per dose once a day.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by infants under 3 months of age, or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, infants under 1 year of age, people who are under a doctor's care, people who are short of folic acid, and people who have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin B1 and B6 supply; neuralgia, muscle and joint pain; eye strain; mouth symptoms
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Infants under 3 months; low folic acid; dye allergy

groups.title: Analgesic Tablet for Neuralgia and Back Pain
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for neuralgia, low back pain and stiff shoulders.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 2 times a day, taken when pain or an attack occurs.
groups.caution: Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: an infant who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; young children and children aged 14 years and under; a person with an allergic constitution or who has had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); a person with liver, kidney or thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; a person who is physically weak or has a high fever; an older person; a woman who is or may be pregnant; or a breastfeeding woman.

summaryTable.Use: Neuralgia, low back pain, stiff shoulders
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 14 years and under; chickenpox or influenza; drug allergy
